title: Density: Why Things Float or Sink
summary: How much mass is packed into a space, and why a steel ship floats while a steel nail sinks.

cbse.chapter: Curiosity Ch 9: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents and Solutions (density)
Gravitation: floatation, density and relative density

objectives: I can calculate density using density = mass ÷ volume, with correct units.
I can predict whether an object floats or sinks by comparing densities.
I can use the particle model to explain differences in density.
misconceptions: Heavy objects always sink and light objects always float.
1 kg of iron is heavier than 1 kg of cotton.
